plan: axios 1.14.1 is flagged as malware. Do not install it.

answer:
Target:   axios/axios @ 9f0f4dd · checked 2026-11-22
Decision: 🔴 Do not adopt — Do not use: malicious release
Confidence: high — The malware listing is direct evidence from two sources that answered, and it alone decides the verdict. The latest release was not checked.

Do not install axios 1.14.1: it is a published malicious release. Choose a different, clean version,
such as the latest 1.21.1, after checking it for vulnerabilities. If 1.14.1 is already installed
anywhere, treat that system as compromised.

Follow-up
 • Is axios 1.14.1 (or 0.30.4) already installed anywhere in your systems?

Why
 🔴 Security: Malicious release: 1.14.1 (GHSA-fw8c-xr5c-95f9, MAL-2026-2307). (CRA Art. 13(5))
   • Version 1.14.1 is a known malicious release (GHSA-fw8c-xr5c-95f9, MAL-2026-2307): do not
     install it.
     "Malicious code in axios (npm)" → https://osv.dev/vulnerability/MAL-2026-2307 ✔
   • Version 1.14.1 of axios is listed as malicious software, so installing it in production could
     compromise your systems.
     "Malware in axios" → https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fw8c-xr5c-95f9 ✔
   • The registry has removed version 1.14.1, which commonly happens with malicious releases. Any
     copy already installed should be treated as compromised.
     "version 1.14.1 is no longer on npm (removed; this often happens to malicious releases)" → https://github.com/axios/axios ✔
 🟢 Licence: MIT licence: permissive, keep the copyright notice.
   • axios uses the permissive MIT licence, so you may use it in a commercial backend if you keep
     the copyright and licence notice.
     "Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy of this software" → https://github.com/axios/axios/blob/9f0f4ddfe72b4c06afafe1a658e6ee53d35b5760/LICENSE#L3 ✔
 🟢 Maintenance: Active repository, not archived, recent commits and releases.
   • The axios repository is actively maintained and not archived. The latest release, 1.21.1, came
     out on 2026-11-09.
     ""head_commit_date": "2026-11-18T05:08:24Z"" → https://github.com/axios/axios ✔

What to do next
 1. Do not install 1.14.1. If it is in any lockfile, build or server, remove it and treat that
   environment as compromised: rotate secrets and review the machines.
     Source: "Malware in axios"
     → https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fw8c-xr5c-95f9
 2. Pin a clean version, for example the latest 1.21.1, only after it has been checked for known
   vulnerabilities, and use a lockfile.
     Source: ""head_commit_date": "2026-11-18T05:08:24Z""
     → https://github.com/axios/axios
 3. Check whether version 0.30.4 is also in use, because the same malware advisory lists it too.
     Source: "Malware in axios"
     → https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fw8c-xr5c-95f9
